review.questionCheck: The unique positive-integer solution is \((x,y)=(2,13)\), so the least sum is 15, choice E. The stem and key agree; no figures or conflicting grading status are supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. Both useful routes are retained: bounded search with parity and congruence modulo 22. The latter matches the supplied LIVE and Random Math arguments; no further route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Integer-equation solving is correctly assessed. Modular congruence is appropriately confined to the alternative method, since the search method does not require it.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Positivity gives \(57x\le378\), hence \(1\le x\le6\). Parity restricts x to 2, 4, and 6. The residuals 286, 172, and 58 have the stated remainders 0, 18, and 14 modulo 22. Only \(x=2\) works, yielding \(y=13\); the search is exhaustive.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The LIVE positivity bound is correctly credited. The parity reduction and explicit bounded search are an original development of that bound, honestly labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move is motivated, and every table entry is justified by an explicit division identity. Uniqueness correctly explains why this sum is the minimum.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:integer-diophantine-equations precisely covers finite bounds, divisibility tests, and completeness. A separate node is unnecessary for the elementary parity consequence.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Reduction gives \(13x\equiv4\pmod{22}\). Since \(13\cdot17\equiv1\pmod{22}\), multiplication yields \(x\equiv68\equiv2\pmod{22}\). The positive bound \(1\le x\le6\) leaves only 2, and substitution gives 13. Thus the solution and minimum sum are unique.
